subtopics.title: Motion — Graphs, Definitions and the Three Equations

questions.question: Distance and displacement differ in that displacement is:
options: The straight line from start to finish, with a direction — a vector
The full winding path length — a scalar

questions.question: A minibus accelerates from rest at 3 m/s² for 4 s. Its final velocity is:
The same minibus's displacement, from Δx = ut + ½at², is:
On a velocity-time graph, displacement is found from:
options: The highest point of the graph
The intercept on the velocity axis
The area between the graph and the time axis

subtopics.title: Energy — the Ledger That Never Lies

questions.question: A 5 kg ball rests 8 m above the ground (reference at ground). Its mechanical energy is:
Halfway down at 4 m, the ball's kinetic energy is 196 J, so its speed is:
Because the mass cancels in ½mv² = mgh, a 50 kg drum dropped from the same 8 m lands at:
options: The same 12,52 m/s as the 5 kg ball
One tenth of the ball's speed
A speed that depends on its shape only

questions.question: The phrase "ignore air resistance" in a question is:
options: A hint that the answer is zero
A warning that energy is not conserved
Your licence to use E k1 + E p1 = E k2 + E p2

subtopics.title: Electricity — Charge, Current and Potential Difference

questions.question: A sphere carries −4,8 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. With the electron charge at 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the excess electrons number:
Identical spheres at +8 nC and −2 nC touch and separate. Each then carries:
20 coulombs pass a point in 5 seconds. The current is:
30 J are transferred as 2 C pass through a resistor. The potential difference across it is:

subtopics.title: Series, Parallel and the Magnetic Field

questions.question: An 18 V battery drives a 3 Ω and a 6 Ω resistor in SERIES. The current is:
The same resistors in PARALLEL across the 18 V battery draw branch currents of:
options: 3 A and 6 A, totalling 9 A from the battery

questions.question: The parallel combination's effective resistance, 18 V ÷ 9 A = 2 Ω, is:
options: Smaller than the smallest branch — always

questions.question: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines run:
options: In closed circles around the middle
Crossing each other at the poles
From north to south, never crossing

subtopics.title: The Logbook, the Wallet and the Water Pipe

questions.question: In the road-trip picture, the odometer and the straight home-to-destination arrow stand for:
The 5 kg ball's wallet reads 392 + 0 at the top. Halfway down it must read:
In the water-pipe picture of a circuit, the battery's emf is:
options: The amount of water in the loop

questions.question: In the pipe picture, series resistors are narrow sections one after another, so:
options: The same flow threads through all of them — same current everywhere
Each section gets its own separate stream
The pressure is the same across each section
The flow increases at each section

questions.question: Opening a second parallel channel makes the combined resistance:
options: Larger, because there is more pipe
Smaller than either branch — the flow has an easier total path

questions.question: A second bulb is added IN PARALLEL with the first. The first bulb:
options: Goes dimmer, because the current is shared
Keeps its brightness — it still spans the full emf — while the battery supplies more current

questions.question: A second bulb is added IN SERIES with the first. Both bulbs:
options: Brighten, because there are more bulbs
Dim, because total resistance rose and the shared current fell

subtopics.title: The Trap List and the Final Check

questions.question: Using g = 10 instead of 9,8 turns the ball's 392 J into:
The one question that sorts every circuit into series or parallel is:
options: Are the wires long or short?

questions.question: The correct placement of the two meters is:
options: Both in series with the component
Ammeter in parallel; voltmeter in series
Both in parallel across the battery
Ammeter in series — a turnstile; voltmeter in parallel — a comparer

questions.question: The "second route" habit means:
options: Answering every question twice on separate pages
Skipping the check to save time
Confirming an answer by an independent method — graph area against equation, audit against ledger
Always using the longest available method
